clue.text: Unimaginative material rotten play!

parts.note: matter is physical material or substance
food gone off is rotten
an act is a part of a play, a stage piece

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a dull drama as rotten stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosaic, literal-minded person or remark lacks imagination.

clue.text: Snake to stop on the road

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A driver is told to brake for a snake crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-like bitumen surfacing is what lies on top of a road.

clue.text: Initially teachers half heartedly comfort valued servant

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word teachers
the heart of the synonym is a double letter, and only half of that pair is kept

parts.note: to reassure someone is to comfort them

explanation.surface: Teachers offer lukewarm comfort to a loyal employee.
explanation.walkthrough: REASSURE has SS at its centre; 'half heartedly' drops one S to leave REASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure is an informal word for a much prized helper or employee.

clue.text: Kick oneself for storing small device

indicators.note: storing means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: to rue is to regret, to kick oneself
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone regrets keeping a tiny gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A device in the sense of a trick or stratagem is a piece of cunning.

clue.text: Stoker and cashiers shack

parts.note: to cashier is to dismiss from service, to fire
a hovel is a shack

explanation.surface: A boiler-man and the bank clerks share a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire shovel is the implement used to feed or stoke a fire.

clue.text: Worn out during an evil uprising

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ill means evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: People are exhausted in the course of a wicked revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' looks like a link word, but here it means the reversed piece goes inside, between the two letters of 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is an informal phrase for exhausted.

clue.text: Quartet entering contest that's of little significance

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a trial is a contest of skill, as in sheepdog trials
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A foursome joins a competition that hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling is unimportant and of slight consequence.

clue.text: Mr Salmon pursues credit for skewer

parts.note: a cock is a male fish, so a male salmon is a cock salmon
to tail is to follow or pursue
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A gentleman named Salmon chases payment for a kebab spike.
explanation.definitionFit: The little pick used to spear olives or cheese cubes at parties is a small skewer.

clue.text: Coppers sealing off resonant performance

parts.note: coppers are small coins, loose change
ringing an area is encircling or cordoning it off

explanation.surface: Police officers close off a booming show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like the police; it is copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-ringers perform rounds of permutations on a peal of bells, a sonorous display.

clue.text: The late news omits St Harry

indicators.note: omits means the named letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: stop press is late news added to a paper after printing began
taken as written

explanation.surface: The latest news bulletin leaves out a saint called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is the verb, to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or persecute, as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Hair gel developed for explorer

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A hair product was invented for an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Raleigh sailed to the Americas as an Elizabethan adventurer and coloniser.

clue.text: King provisions poet…

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
eats is informal for food, provisions

explanation.surface: A monarch supplies food to a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic versifier.

clue.text: … when alliance catches cold in capital

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: catches means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a union is an alliance
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The partnership caught a chill in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: Friends accepting rascal is in France getting reused manuscript

indicators.note: accepting means taking another piece inside

parts.note: pals are friends
an imp is a little rascal
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Mates take in a scamp who is in France for a recycled document.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment scraped clean and written over again.

clue.text: Electrical supplier and Loretta ran off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Loretta made off with a generator.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternator is a generator producing alternating current, supplying power.

clue.text: This is left in potter's equipment

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a snooker player who pots balls uses a cue

explanation.surface: Something is left among a ceramicist's tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' suggests clay; it is a snooker or pool player who pots balls. 'This' refers to the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'This' points at the very thing being read: a crossword hint.

clue.text: Cat's coat badly clipped

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A cat's fur has been poorly trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato notes or speech are short and detached, cut off sharply.

clue.text: Fate keeps Bob at sea

indicators.note: keeps means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money

explanation.surface: Destiny keeps a man named Bob out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in pre-1971 British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is being bewildered, adrift and without direction.

clue.text: Silly asses endlessly carry mollusc

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word asses is cut

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: Foolish donkeys keep hauling a shellfish around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims ASSES to ASSE, and 'Silly' rearranges it as SEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea slug is a marine gastropod without a shell, a kind of soft-bodied invertebrate.

clue.text: Little girl tolerated tenor opposed to amateurs

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
let means allowed, tolerated
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A young girl put up with a singer hostile to dabblers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilettanti are dabblers in the arts who lack professional commitment.

clue.text: First of injections in bottom? Not at all!

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: nether means lower, at the bottom

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word injections

explanation.surface: A patient refuses a first jab in the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither, as a reply, means 'not either one', a refusal of both options.

clue.text: Tory leader managed a month in church

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leader of the word Tory is its first letter
to run something is to manage it
Sept is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: The Conservative chief ran things for a month in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the cross-arm of a cruciform church building.

clue.text: Cancel loan that's now in credit

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan on wages
CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A borrower writes off a debt now that the account is in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to call it off informally.

clue.text: Grasp many fish

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fisherman grabs a big haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to hold on tightly.

clue.text: Beastly home earl finds an eyesore

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, an animal's home

explanation.surface: A nobleman finds a pig's pen ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' is taken literally: a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: A recoil released an amount of energy

indicators.note: released suggests the letters are freed and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A gun's kick lets loose a burst of force.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a unit of heat, used to measure food's energy value.

clue.text: Drink's a feature of the seminar

parts.note: tea is a drink; the 's is a link
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Tea is a regular part of the discussion class.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture-and-debate session on a topic, a kind of forum.

clue.text: Follow top management or come to grief

parts.note: to go by a rule is to follow it
the board are a company's directors, its top management

explanation.surface: Obey the bosses or end in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by the board is an idiom for being abandoned or failing.
